name: Can I keep the garage door opening in a converted ADU?

mainEntity.name: If I want the converted unit to look like a studio or guesthouse, can the old garage door opening stay visible from the outside?
mainEntity.text: If I want the converted unit to look like a studio or guesthouse, can the old garage door opening stay visible from the outside?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many homeowners want the converted ADU to retain some of the original garage character, but the exterior treatment has to work with code, insulation, weatherproofing, and neighborhood appearance rules. The large door opening is usually replaced with a framed wall assembly, which can then be designed with windows, siding, stucco, or a new entry door. In some cases, a designer can make the front elevation more attractive by adding architectural features that reduce the “former garage” look. What matters most is that the building envelope becomes fully habitable and energy-efficient. If the garage door remains functional or visually dominant, the space may not be treated as a true living unit. Homeowners should ask how the conversion will affect curb appeal, daylight, privacy, and ventilation before finalizing plans. The best designs usually balance code compliance with a seamless exterior that matches the main house.
acceptedAnswer.description: The garage opening can sometimes be redesigned instead of fully hidden, but the new exterior still must meet building and planning requirements. In most cases, the opening is infilled with framed walls, windows, or a new entry so the space performs as habitable living area rather than garage space.
